title: Convolutional networks
intro: A CNN applies the same learned filter at multiple image locations. One filter can thus detect a local pattern regardless of where it occurs in the image.
focus: Trace image height, width and channels through convolution and pooling.
Count trained parameters and multiplications separately.
Calculate a local response and express the same operation as a matrix product.

terms.feature map: The spatial responses from one filter in a network layer.
terms.stride: The pixel distance between successive placements of the filter window.
terms.pooling: Summarising a local region, for example by taking the maximum in each 2 × 2 window.
terms.logit: A raw class score before conversion into a probability.

sections.title: Calculating output size
sections.html:
A filter sees a window across all input channels and produces one feature map. The number of filters therefore equals the number of output channels. With filter width K, symmetric padding P on each side, stride S and dilation 1, Wut=⌊Winn+2P−KS⌋+1. Use the same formula for height. The floor counts only placements where the whole window fits after padding.

For a 9 × 9 image with 2 channels, three 3 × 3 filters, stride 2 and P = 1, output W = ⌊(9 + 2 − 3)/2⌋ + 1 = 5. The result is 5 × 5 × 3. ReLU changes no dimensions. A 2 × 2 max-pooling operation with stride 2 and no padding gives 2 × 2 × 3, or twelve values when flattened. The remainders at the right and bottom lie outside the windows.

The output-size formula counts valid filter starting positions. With padded width W + 2P, the final possible start is W + 2P − K. Because the first start is zero, one initial window is added to the number of complete steps.

Basic practice · How many starts fit width 5 with kernel 3, stride 1 and no padding?

Start at column zero.

Show answer

Starts 0,1,2 fit. Start 3 would require column 5. Output width is 3.

Application · our practice exercise

Input is 7 × 8, kernel 3 × 3, stride 2, no padding. List starting positions and dimensions. What happens to the final column?

Hint

Use rows and columns indexed from 0. Each window must fit completely.

Show answer

Row starts are 0,2,4 and column starts are 0,2,4. The result is 3 × 3 per filter. The final window covers columns 4–6. Column 7 is unused because start 6 would require column 8.

sections.title: Counting stored weights and computational work
sections.html:
Each filter uses Kh·Kw·Cin weights and optionally one bias. Multiply by Cout to count parameters. In the layer above, (3·3·2 + 1)·3 = 57. The same 57 parameters are reused at every position. Fixed max pooling has no trainable parameters.

The number of multiplications for direct evaluation, however, is Hout·Wout·Cout·Kh·Kw·Cin = 5·5·3·18 = 1350. This counts operations on padding, and counts a multiplication and addition separately. Each output sums 18 products using 17 additions, plus one if bias is added. A fully connected layer from twelve flattened values to four classes would have 12·4 + 4 = 52 parameters.

Separate weights from multiply operations

Apply four 3 × 3 filters to an 8 × 8 image with three channels, unit stride and no padding. Each filter spans all three input channels and has one bias. Six horizontal and six vertical placements fit.

Parameters = 4(3 × 3 × 3 + 1) = 112

How many weight multiplications does the forward pass use?

Check your reasoning

There are 6 × 6 × 4 output values. Each needs 27 weight multiplications, giving 3,888. Reusing the same filter at every location increases the work while keeping its parameter count fixed.

Weight sharing means applying the same feature detector at all spatial positions. More input channels give more weights per detector. More output channels give more detectors. A larger image alone increases how often they are applied.

Basic practice · How many feature maps do four filters produce?

Each filter sums across all input channels.

Show answer

Four feature maps. Input channel count determines each filter's depth, not the number of output maps.

Application · our practice exercise

A 1 × 1 layer maps 8 channels to 3 over 10 × 10 image positions. Can it mix colours, and can it see neighbouring pixels? Calculate parameters and multiplications.

Hint

Each output is a dot product across all channels of one pixel, plus a bias.

Show answer

Three weight rows with eight entries and three biases give 27 parameters. At 100 positions, 100·3·8 = 2400 multiplications are required. The layer mixes channels but has no spatial neighbour in its own receptive field.

sections.title: Calculating responses, activations and class scores
sections.source: L03c_CNNs-FPass, PDF p. 36–61 and 145–154. DLFund_Examples_3-Pre-CNNs, PDF p. 5–7 and 4-Post-CNNs, PDF p. 9–13.
sections.html:
In the usual CNN forward pass, the filter has its stated orientation. For row [3, 1, 4, 2], filter [2, −1], stride 1 and no padding, collect windows [3,1], [1,4], [4,2] as matrix rows. Multiply each row by [2,−1]ᵀ. Responses are [5, −2, 6] before bias. An alternative matrix has rows [2,−1,0,0], [0,2,−1,0], [0,0,2,−1]. Multiplying it by the image row as a column gives the same three results.

With zero bias, ReLU gives [5, 0, 6]. A final classifier computes one logit per class. Softmax of logits [ln 3, ln 2] gives [3/5, 2/5]. If the second class is correct, categorical cross-entropy is −ln(2/5) ≈ 0,916. Loss decreases when the model assigns higher probability to the correct class.

A filter has one weight plane per input channel. Sum responses from all planes and add one bias before activation. Applying ReLU separately to each channel before summing removes negative contributions that should cancel positive ones.

Basic practice · When is bias added to a CNN result?

Distinguish individual channel contributions from the total response.

Show answer

One bias per filter is added to the total sum at every spatial position, before activation.

Application · our practice exercise

Two channel windows are [1,2] and [3,1]. Weights are [2,1] and [−2,1]. Use correlation, bias 2 and ReLU. Find one output.

Hint

Write one sum per channel. How many times should bias be added?

Show answer

The first contribution is 2·1+1·2 = 4. The second is −2·3+1·1 = −5. Before activation, 4−5+2 = 1; after ReLU, it remains 1. Every position in this feature map uses the same weights and bias.

question: An 8 × 8 RGB image passes through five 3 × 3 filters with stride 1, no padding and one bias per filter. Find output shape, parameter count and multiplication count.
hint: Each output value sees 3 × 3 positions in each of three channels.
answer: Width and height are (8 − 3)/1 + 1 = 6. Shape is 6 × 6 × 5. There are (27 + 1)·5 = 140 parameters. The 180 outputs require 27 multiplications each, totalling 4860.
